statement: A solid block is built from unit cubes and measures 4 by 3 by 2. How many unit cubes does it contain?

figure.alt: A rectangular block built from unit cubes, 4 cubes long, 3 cubes deep and 2 cubes tall, drawn so that both layers are visible.

choices.misconception: I added the three measurements together instead of multiplying them.
I counted one layer of 4 by 3 and forgot that the block is two layers tall.
I read the block as 3 by 3 by 2 because the drawing hid the far column.
I counted only the cubes whose faces I could actually see in the picture.

hints: Count one layer, then count the layers.
A solid block is layers of the same size stacked up. Work out how many cubes are in one horizontal layer, then multiply by the number of layers.
One layer is 4 x 3 = 12 cubes and there are 2 layers, so 12 x 2 = 24.

solutions.reliable: One horizontal layer is 4 by 3, which is 12 cubes. The block is 2 layers tall, so it holds 12 x 2 = 24 unit cubes. The transferable idea: counting a layer at a time reaches the cubes you cannot see, and it keeps working when the layers are not all the same size.

whyOnTest: It anchors the layer-by-layer habit before the harder hidden-cube questions where the layers differ in size.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
